title: Grandma’s “Rolling Pin”
synopsis: Grandma raised six outstanding children. This is how she did it!

fullText.simplified:
奶奶的“擀面杖”

    由于父母工作忙，没有时间照顾我，在我六个月的时候，就被父母送到了乡下奶奶家。
    我奶奶是个特别厉害的女人。我爷爷去世得早，奶奶一个人养大了六个子女，而且个个都很优秀：我大伯在政府工作；二伯是当地有名的大夫；大姑是大学教授；小姑是公司老板；我爸爸是老五，是个建筑师；小叔还在上学，是清华大学的博士生。我每次淘气不学习的时候，奶奶都会拿出她的擀面杖，做出要打我的样子，再说一遍她那些子女的光荣历史，脸上都是自豪骄傲的表情。说实话，我听得耳朵都起茧子了。但我心里也很纳闷：“奶奶这个文化水平不高的乡下老太太是怎么培养出那么多出色的孩子的呢？”
    直到奶奶过80大寿的时候，奶奶的“育儿秘籍”才被她说出来。奶奶过生日那天特别热闹。财大气粗的小姑在最好的酒店订了好几十桌酒菜，亲戚朋友来了好多人。大家吃饭喝酒，高兴得不得了。大家纷纷端着酒杯敬奶奶酒。有个人问奶奶：“趁现在大伙儿都在，您老人家给我们讲讲您是怎么教育子女的，让我们学学经验吧！”奶奶听了，微微一笑，在我小姑耳边说了几句，我小姑就离开了。奶奶说：“等老四拿回我要的东西，我再讲。”
    大约过了十几分钟，小姑回来了，她手里拿着一根擀面杖。我一看更奇怪了：“这不是我奶奶擀面条用的吗？把它拿过来干嘛呀？”小姑把擀面杖交给了奶奶，奶奶拿着它大声说：“大伙儿安静一下，你们不是一直好奇我是怎么培养他们六个的吗？今天就给大家讲一讲。你们看这根擀面杖，这是我妈妈的妈妈传下来的，到我这儿快三百年了。你们都知道，我就是靠着它卖面条，养活了六个孩子，供他们吃穿上学的。我妈妈曾经告诉过我，这人啊，就像是做面条前和好的面，你想怎么和就怎么和。但是要想做出好的面条，就要不软不硬正合适。孩子不也是这样吗？想让他成才，做父母的就不能过分溺爱，也不能太暴力，要适度。要不断告诉他什么是对什么是错，什么应该做什么不应该做。”
    大家一听都纷纷点头，奶奶继续说：“面和好了，就该擀面条了。面条好不好，擀面杖很重要。一根又长又光滑的擀面杖能帮助你擀出好吃的面条。养孩子也一样啊！想让孩子走正道，就需要不断地敲打他们，发现问题要及时指出来。你们问问我这六个孩子，他们哪个没挨过我这擀面杖的打。我这又长又光滑的擀面杖就是一把尺子，它随时提醒孩子们哪里做对了，哪里做错了。”
    爸爸、大伯他们听了奶奶的话，都点头同意。大伯说：“是啊，我小时候可讨厌这根擀面杖了。我记得我9岁那年拿了邻居张奶奶家的鸡蛋，也是被我妈妈用这根擀面杖打了。她老人家说这根擀面杖代表的是我们家人的勤劳，它代表着我们家人的品质，我们都应该像它一样正直、善良。”
    在场的每一个人都默默点头，我也明白了奶奶的擀面杖重要的意义。奶奶说不出高深的话语，但是她用老百姓最朴实的行动证明了家庭教育的重要。
fullText.traditional:
奶奶的“擀麵杖”

    由於父母工作忙，沒有時間照顧我，在我六個月的時候，就被父母送到了鄉下奶奶家。
    我奶奶是個特別厲害的女人。我爺爺去世得早，奶奶一個人養大了六個子女，而且個個都很優秀：我大伯在政府工作；二伯是當地有名的大夫；大姑是大學教授；小姑是公司老闆；我爸爸是老五，是個建築師；小叔還在上學，是清華大學的博士生。我每次淘氣不學習的時候，奶奶都會拿出她的擀麵杖，做出要打我的樣子，再說一遍她那些子女的光榮歷史，臉上都是自豪驕傲的表情。說實話，我聽得耳朵都起繭子了。但我心裡也很納悶：“奶奶這個文化水平不高的鄉下老太太是怎麼培養出那麼多出色的孩子的呢？”
    直到奶奶過80大壽的時候，奶奶的“育兒秘籍”才被她說出來。奶奶過生日那天特別熱鬧。財大氣粗的小姑在最好的酒店訂了好幾十桌酒菜，親戚朋友來了好多人。大家吃飯喝酒，高興得不得了。大家紛紛端著酒杯敬奶奶酒。有個人問奶奶：“趁現在大伙兒都在，您老人家給我們講講您是怎麼教育子女的，讓我們學學經驗吧！”奶奶聽了，微微一笑，在我小姑耳邊說了幾句，我小姑就離開了。奶奶說：“等老四拿回我要的東西，我再講。”
    大約過了十幾分鐘，小姑回來了，她手裡拿著一根擀麵杖。我一看更奇怪了：“這不是我奶奶擀麵條用的嗎？把它拿過來幹嘛呀？”小姑把擀麵杖交給了奶奶，奶奶拿著它大聲說：“大伙兒安靜一下，你們不是一直好奇我是怎麼培養他們六個的嗎？今天就給大家講一講。你們看這根擀麵杖，這是我媽媽的媽媽傳下來的，到我這兒快三百年了。你們都知道，我就是靠著它賣麵條，養活了六個孩子，供他們吃穿上學的。我媽媽曾經告訴過我，這人啊，就像是做麵條前和好的麵，你想怎麼和就怎麼和。但是要想做出好的麵條，就要不軟不硬正合適。孩子不也是這樣嗎？想讓他成才，做父母的就不能過分溺愛，也不能太暴力，要適度。要不斷告訴他什麼是對什麼是錯，什麼應該做什麼不應該做。”
    大家一聽都紛紛點頭，奶奶繼續說：“麵和好了，就該擀麵條了。麵條好不好，擀麵杖很重要。一根又長又光滑的擀麵杖能幫助你擀出好吃的麵條。養孩子也一樣啊！想讓孩子走正道，就需要不斷地敲打他們，發現問題要及時指出來。你們問問我這六個孩子，他們哪個沒挨過我這擀麵杖的打。我這又長又光滑的擀麵杖就是一把尺子，它隨時提醒孩子們哪裡做對了，哪裡做錯了。”
    爸爸、大伯他們聽了奶奶的話，都點頭同意。大伯說：“是啊，我小時候可討厭這根擀麵杖了。我記得我9歲那年拿了鄰居張奶奶家的雞蛋，也是被我媽媽用這根擀麵杖打了。她老人家說這根擀麵杖代表的是我們家人的勤勞，它代表著我們家人的品質，我們都應該像它一樣正直、善良。”
    在場的每一個人都默默點頭，我也明白了奶奶的擀麵杖重要的意義。奶奶說不出高深的話語，但是她用老百姓最樸實的行動證明了家庭教育的重要。

sentences.pinyin: nǐ men dōu zhī dào wǒ jiù shì kào zhe tā mài miàn tiáo yǎng huo le liù ge hái zi gōng tā men chī chuān shàng xué de
sentences.english: It was handed down by my mother’s mother. It’s been handed down for almost 300 years.

sentences.simplified: 我妈妈曾经告诉过我，这人啊，就像是做面条前和好的面，你想怎么和就怎么和。
sentences.traditional: 我媽媽曾經告訴過我，這人啊，就像是做麵條前和好的麵，你想怎麼和就怎麼和。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ mā ma céng jīng gào su guò wǒ zhè rén a jiù xiàng shì zuò miàn tiáo qián huò hǎo de miàn nǐ xiǎng zěn me huò jiù zěn me huò
sentences.english: As you all know, I depended on it to sell noodles and support my six children, providing them with food, clothes, and schooling.

sentences.simplified: 但是要想做出好的面条，就要不软不硬正合适。孩子不也是这样吗？
sentences.traditional: 但是要想做出好的麵條，就要不軟不硬正合適。孩子不也是這樣嗎？
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì yào xiǎng zuò chū hǎo de miàn tiáo jiù yào bù ruǎn bú yìng zhèng hé shì hái zi bù yě shì zhè yàng ma
sentences.english: My mom used to tell me that people are just like kneading dough to make noodles. You can mix it however you want.

sentences.simplified: 想让他成才，做父母的就不能过分溺爱，也不能太暴力，要适度。
sentences.traditional: 想讓他成才，做父母的就不能過分溺愛，也不能太暴力，要適度。
sentences.pinyin: xiǎng ràng tā chéng cái zuò fù mǔ de jiù bù néng guò fèn nì ài yě bù néng tài bào lì yào shì dù
sentences.english: But to make good noodles, it can’t be too soft or too hard. It has to be just right. Isn’t it the same with children?

sentences.simplified: 要不断告诉他什么是对什么是错，什么应该做什么不应该做。”
sentences.traditional: 要不斷告訴他什麼是對什麼是錯，什麼應該做什麼不應該做。”
sentences.pinyin: yào bú duàn gào su tā shén me shì duì shén me shì cuò shén me yīng gāi zuò shén me bù yīng gāi zuò
sentences.english: If you want them to make something of themselves, parents can’t spoil them too much, nor be too violent. It has to be in moderation.
You have to keep telling them what’s right and what’s wrong, what they should do and what they shouldn’t do.”

sentences.simplified: 大家一听都纷纷点头，
sentences.traditional: 大家一聽都紛紛點頭，
sentences.pinyin: dà jiā yì tīng dōu fēn fēn diǎn tóu

sentences.simplified: 奶奶继续说：“面和好了，就该擀面条了。
sentences.traditional: 奶奶繼續說：“麵和好了，就該擀麵條了。
sentences.pinyin: nǎi nai jì xù shuō miàn huò hǎo le jiù gāi gǎn miàn tiáo le
sentences.english: One by one, everyone nodded when they heard this.

sentences.simplified: 面条好不好，擀面杖很重要。
sentences.traditional: 麵條好不好，擀麵杖很重要。
sentences.pinyin: miàn tiáo hǎo bù hǎo gǎn miàn zhàng hěn zhòng yào
sentences.english: Grandma continued, “When you have finished kneading the dough, it’s time to make the noodles.

sentences.simplified: 一根又长又光滑的擀面杖能帮助你擀出好吃的面条。养孩子也一样啊！
sentences.traditional: 一根又長又光滑的擀麵杖能幫助你擀出好吃的麵條。養孩子也一樣啊！
sentences.pinyin: yì gēn yòu cháng yòu guāng huá de gǎn miàn zhàng néng bāng zhù nǐ gǎn chū hǎo chī de miàn tiáo yǎng hái zi yě yí yàng a
sentences.english: The rolling pin is important for making good noodles.

sentences.simplified: 想让孩子走正道，就需要不断地敲打他们，发现问题要及时指出来。
sentences.traditional: 想讓孩子走正道，就需要不斷地敲打他們，發現問題要及時指出來。
sentences.pinyin: xiǎng ràng hái zi zǒu zhèng dào jiù xū yào bú duàn de qiāo dǎ tā men fā xiàn wèn tí yào jí shí zhǐ chu lai
sentences.english: A long and smooth rolling pin will help you make delicious noodles. Raising children is the same!

sentences.simplified: 你们问问我这六个孩子，他们哪个没挨过我这擀面杖的打。
sentences.traditional: 你們問問我這六個孩子，他們哪個沒挨過我這擀麵杖的打。
sentences.pinyin: nǐ men wèn wen wǒ zhè liù ge hái zi tā men nǎ ge méi ái guò wǒ zhè gǎn miàn zhàng de dǎ
sentences.english: If you want to keep your children on the right path, you need to keep beating them and pointing out problems when you find them.

sentences.simplified: 我这又长又光滑的擀面杖就是一把尺子，
sentences.traditional: 我這又長又光滑的擀麵杖就是一把尺子，
sentences.pinyin: wǒ zhè yòu cháng yòu guāng huá de gǎn miàn zhàng jiù shì yì bǎ chǐ zi
sentences.english: Ask my six children, which of them has not been beaten with my rolling pin.

sentences.simplified: 它随时提醒孩子们哪里做对了，哪里做错了。”
sentences.traditional: 它隨時提醒孩子們哪裡做對了，哪裡做錯了。”
sentences.pinyin: tā suí shí tí xǐng hái zi men nǎ lǐ zuò duì le nǎ lǐ zuò cuò le
sentences.english: This long and smooth rolling pin of mine is a ruler, ..
.. always there to remind the children when they did something right and when they did something wrong.”

sentences.simplified: 爸爸、大伯他们听了奶奶的话，都点头同意。
sentences.traditional: 爸爸、大伯他們聽了奶奶的話，都點頭同意。
sentences.pinyin: bà ba dà bó tā men tīng le nǎi nai de huà dōu diǎn tóu tóng yì

sentences.simplified: 大伯说：“是啊，我小时候可讨厌这根擀面杖了。
sentences.traditional: 大伯說：“是啊，我小時候可討厭這根擀麵杖了。
sentences.pinyin: dà bó shuō shì a wǒ xiǎo shí hou kě tǎo yàn zhè gēn gǎn miàn zhàng le
sentences.english: Dad and my oldest uncle nodded in agreement when they heard what Grandma said.

sentences.simplified: 我记得我9岁那年拿了邻居张奶奶家的鸡蛋，也是被我妈妈用这根擀面杖打了。
sentences.traditional: 我記得我9歲那年拿了鄰居張奶奶家的雞蛋，也是被我媽媽用這根擀麵杖打了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ jì de wǒ 1 suì nà nián ná le lín jū zhāng nǎi nai jiā de jī dàn yě shì bèi wǒ mā ma yòng zhè gēn gǎn miàn zhàng dǎ le
sentences.english: My oldest uncle said, “Yes, I hated this rolling pin when I was a child.

sentences.simplified: 她老人家说这根擀面杖代表的是我们家人的勤劳，
sentences.traditional: 她老人家說這根擀麵杖代表的是我們家人的勤勞，
sentences.pinyin: tā lǎo rén jiā shuō zhè gēn gǎn miàn zhàng dài biǎo de shì wǒ men jiā rén de qín láo
sentences.english: I remember when I was 9 years old, I took eggs from our neighbor Grandma Zhang’s house, and my mom used this rolling pin to beat me.

sentences.simplified: 它代表着我们家人的品质，我们都应该像它一样正直、善良。”
sentences.traditional: 它代表著我們家人的品質，我們都應該像它一樣正直、善良。”
sentences.pinyin: tā dài biǎo zhe wǒ men jiā rén de pǐn zhì wǒ men dōu yīng gāi xiàng tā yí yàng zhèng zhí shàn liáng
sentences.english: She said that this rolling pin represents the hard work of our family.
It represents the character of our family, and we should all be as upright and decent as it is.”

sentences.simplified: 在场的每一个人都默默点头，我也明白了奶奶的擀面杖重要的意义。
sentences.traditional: 在場的每一個人都默默點頭，我也明白了奶奶的擀麵杖重要的意義。
sentences.pinyin: zài chǎng de měi yí ge rén dōu mò mò diǎn tóu wǒ yě míng bai le nǎi nai de gǎn miàn zhàng zhòng yào de yì yì

sentences.simplified: 奶奶说不出高深的话语，但是她用老百姓最朴实的行动证明了家庭教育的重要。
sentences.traditional: 奶奶說不出高深的話語，但是她用老百姓最樸實的行動證明了家庭教育的重要。
sentences.pinyin: nǎi nai shuō bù chū gāo shēn de huà yǔ dàn shì tā yòng lǎo bǎi xìng zuì pǔ shí de xíng dòng zhèng míng le jiā tíng jiào yù de zhòng yào
sentences.english: Everyone present nodded silently, and I also understood the important meaning of Grandma’s rolling pin.

sentence_translations: Grandma’s “Rolling Pin”
Since my parents were busy with work and didn’t have time to take care of me, ..
.. my parents sent me to my grandma’s house in the countryside when I was 6 months old.
My grandma is a really incredible woman.
My grandpa died a long time ago. My grandma raised six children by herself, and they were all outstanding.
My oldest uncle works for the government, and my second uncle is a famous local doctor.
My oldest aunt is a university professor, and my youngest aunt is the boss of a company.
My father is the fifth oldest and an architect.
My youngest uncle is still studying. He is a Ph.D. student at Tsinghua University.
Every time I was naughty and didn’t study, ..
.. my grandma would take out her rolling pin and act like she was going to beat me.
Then she would tell the whole glorious history of those children of hers, her face full of pride.
To be honest, I was sick of hearing about it. But I was also puzzled:
“How did Grandma, an old lady from the countryside with a low level of education, raise so many outstanding children?”
It was not until Grandma’s 80th birthday that she talked about her “secret to raising children”.
Grandma’s birthday was bustling with noise and excitement.
My rich and overbearing younger aunt ordered dozens of tables with food and drink at the best restaurant.
Many relatives and friends came. Everyone was eating and drinking and was extremely happy.
Then, one by one, everyone held their wine glasses with both hands to toast Grandma.
Someone asked Grandma, ..
.. “Now that we are all here, take this opportunity to tell us how you raised your children so that we can learn from your experience!”
When Grandma heard that, she smiled slightly and whispered something in my youngest aunt’s ear, who then left.
Grandma said, “I’ll talk about it when my fourth child has brought me what I want.”
After about 10 minutes, my youngest aunt came back with a rolling pin in her hand.
I was even more baffled when I saw that: “Isn’t that what Grandma uses to make noodles? Why bring it here?”
My youngest aunt handed the rolling pin to Grandma, who took it and said loudly, ..
.. “Everyone be quiet. Haven’t you always been curious about how I raised the six of them?
Let me tell you about it today. Look at this rolling pin.
It was handed down by my mother’s mother. It’s been handed down for almost 300 years.
As you all know, I depended on it to sell noodles and support my six children, providing them with food, clothes, and schooling.
My mom used to tell me that people are just like kneading dough to make noodles. You can mix it however you want.
But to make good noodles, it can’t be too soft or too hard. It has to be just right. Isn’t it the same with children?
If you want them to make something of themselves, parents can’t spoil them too much, nor be too violent. It has to be in moderation.
You have to keep telling them what’s right and what’s wrong, what they should do and what they shouldn’t do.”
One by one, everyone nodded when they heard this.
Grandma continued, “When you have finished kneading the dough, it’s time to make the noodles.
The rolling pin is important for making good noodles.
A long and smooth rolling pin will help you make delicious noodles. Raising children is the same!
If you want to keep your children on the right path, you need to keep beating them and pointing out problems when you find them.
Ask my six children, which of them has not been beaten with my rolling pin.
This long and smooth rolling pin of mine is a ruler, ..
.. always there to remind the children when they did something right and when they did something wrong.”
Dad and my oldest uncle nodded in agreement when they heard what Grandma said.
My oldest uncle said, “Yes, I hated this rolling pin when I was a child.
I remember when I was 9 years old, I took eggs from our neighbor Grandma Zhang’s house, and my mom used this rolling pin to beat me.
She said that this rolling pin represents the hard work of our family.
It represents the character of our family, and we should all be as upright and decent as it is.”
Everyone present nodded silently, and I also understood the important meaning of Grandma’s rolling pin.
Grandma can’t say profound words, but she proved the importance of family education with the simple actions of an ordinary person.
